USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                 U5-65
CREATE/MODIFY LABEL                                                    CHAPTER 5


CREATE/    CREATE/MODIFY LABEL is a full-screen, menu-driven command
           which allows you to create label form ( .lbl) files using the fields
MODIFY     specified in the current database file or in other related database
LABEL      files .

Syntax     CREATE/MODIFY LABEL < filename > /?

Defaults   Unless you specify otherwise, dBASE III PLUS creates the file with
           the .lbl extension . If a catalog is open and SET CATALOG is ON, the
           label file is added to the catalog .

Usage      You use the CREATE LABEL command to create a new label
           form file . You specify the size of the label you want to create and
           the number of printed lines on each label . These values should
           match the label forms or paper on which you want to print .
           You use MODIFY LABEL to modify an existing label form file . If
           you use the catalog query (?) with the MODIFY LABEL command,
           you will be prompted to select a file from the list of label form files
           already in the catalog .
           Using CREATE or MODIFY LABEL, you specify the information you
           want on each label . For each line on the label, you specify a dBASE
           expression, which may combine character strings, fields, and func-
           tions . The fields you specify in the expression must be from the cur-
           rent database file or in other related database files (as in a view
           file) .
           After you finish creating the label form and saving the label file, you
           can display or print labels with the LABEL command . You can use
           a filter condition or filter query ( .qry) file to specify particular
           records you want to appear on labels .
           While you are creating the format for labels, you can toggle a cur-
           sor navigation menu on or off the screen by pressing F1 . This menu
           describes the operations you can perform, and the keys you can use .

Options    The CREATE/MODIFY LABEL menu bar displays three choices :
           Options, Contents, and Exit .

Options    The Options Menu allows you to determine the size and number of
           lines printed on labels .



U5-66                                                       USING dBASE III PLUS
COMMANDS                                                 CREATE/MODIFY LABEL

                  The Predefined size option lets you choose one of five standard
                  label sizes:

                            Width       Height       Number of labels across
                            3-1/2"      15/16"       1
                            3-1/2"      15/16"       2
                            3-1/2"      15/16"       3
                            4"          1-7/16"      1
                            3-2/10"     11/12"       3    (Cheshire style)
                                            Table 5-1 Standard label sizes

                  When you choose a standard label size, dBASE III PLUS automati-
                  cally fills in values for the remaining options . Otherwise, you can
                  adjust these values to suit your needs, entering a new value or using
                  the T or y arrow keys to change the values . The settings you enter
                  should match the label forms or paper on which you are printing .
                  Each of the options has a set range of allowable values .

                   Option                                              Range
                   Label width                                         1-120 characters
                   Label height                                        1-16 lines
                   Left margin (offset by SET MARGIN TO                0-120 characters
                      setting)
                   Lines between labels                                0-16 lines
                   Spaces between labels                               0-120 characters
                   Labels across page                                  1-5 labels .
                                      Table 5-2 Option Menu range specifications


                  The maximum width of all labels is 250 characters .
                  The LEFT margin option is added to the current setting of the SET
                  MARGIN TO command . For example, if you enter a left margin of
                  5, and SET MARGIN was previously set to 11, your labels will print
                  with a left margin of 16 .




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                      U5-67
CREATE/MODIFY LABEL                                                         CHAPTER 5



Contents   You design the layout of the label through the Contents Menu . You
           can enter as many lines as you specified in the Options Menu . For
           each line on the label, specify any valid dBASE expression, which
           may combine character strings, fields, and functions . The fields you
           specify on the label form must be from the current database file or
           from other related files .
           Press    to begin entering fields or an expression on each line in
           the Contents Menu . When you're entering more than one field on a
           line, you need to separate the fields with a comma or plus sign . If
           you use a comma, dBASE III PLUS removes trailing blank spaces in
           a field and then inserts one blank space before the next field or
           character on the label . A plus sign does not remove trailing blanks .
           As you enter an expression and reach the end of an entry line in the
           Contents Menu, characters in the expression scroll horizontally .
           You use the E- and - keys to move the cursor back and forth on
           the line . If you want to see the entire line all at once, you can press
           Ctrl-PgDn to make your entry on a full-length editing line at the bot-
           tom of the screen . When you're finished with an entry on this line,
           press Ctrl-PgUp to return to the Contents Menu . You can use this
           zoom option to create or edit expressions for each line of the label
           form.
           Press F1 Help if you're not sure which keys you can use while in the
           Contents Menu . While you're entering an expression, you can also
           press F10 to display a list of field names from the database file in
           use or fields specified by a view file . You select a field by highlight-
           ing it on the field list and pressing ~--~. The field automatically
           appears in the label expression you're entering . You can use this
           feature as a shortcut to specifying fields, or as a reminder of the
           fields in the file .
           When creating a label, you can use functions in an expression to
           combine fields and character strings on a line . For example, to put
           a comma on a line without having a space between a field and the
           comma (as in Los Angeles, CA 90049), you could enter the follow-
           ing expression:

             Label contents 1 :TRIM(City)   + ',',State,tipcode




U5-68                                                             USING dBASE III PLUS
COMMANDS                                         CREATE/MODIFY LABEL

                  The TRIM() function removes all trailing blanks, and the plus sign
                  puts the comma immediately after City . The commas before and
                  after State insert blank spaces .

Exit              The Save option saves the label file . The Abandon option abandons
                  the creation of a new label file or changes made to an existing one .
                  If you're creating or modifying a label file and want to abandon the
                  file, you can press Esc. You are prompted to abandon your work on
                  the label file, or resume it .

See Also          LABEL, TRIM()




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                              U5-69
CREATE/MODIFY QUERY                                                     CHAPTER 5


CREATE/    CREATE/MODIFY QUERY creates or modifies a file which specifies
           conditions that records in a database file must match to be
MODIFY     accessed .
QUERY
Syntax     CREATE/MODIFY QUERY < .qry filename > /?

Defaults   Unless otherwise specified, dBASE III PLUS supplies the .qry exten-
           sion . If a catalog is open and SET CATALOG in ON, the query file is
           added to the catalog .

Usage      CREATE QUERY and MODIFY QUERY are full-screen, menu-driven
           commands that create or modify a filter (query) file associated with
           a database or view file . A query file allows only the records that
           meet the specified conditions to be displayed when commands are
           executed after the query file is set up .
           You use CREATE QUERY to build a new query file . You use
           MODIFY QUERY to modify an existing query file . If you want to
           modify an existing query file, and a catalog file is active, you can
           use MODIFY QUERY ?. This displays a list of .qry files associated
           with the currently selected database file or view files .
           After you create a query file and exit with the Save option, dBASE
           III PLUS automatically activates the new or modified query file . To
           deactivate the filter, use SET FILTER TO 4 . To activate an existing
           query file, use the SET FILTER TO FILE < .qry > /? command .
           You can specify up to seven separate conditions in a query file .
           Each condition specifies a test for fields in the database file(s) for
           which the query file is constructed .
           When you are constructing a query file, you first enter a field name .
           Then you specify an operator specific to the data type of the field
           name . Finally, you specify the condition that the field needs to
           match . If you want to add additional conditions, specify a Connect
           operator - .AND., .OR ., .AND . .NOT., or .OR . .NOT. When you're
           all finished, select No combination .
           An example of a condition which you can construct in a query file
           is :
           TRAVELCODE _ 'CI10' .AND . PAID Is False




U5-70                                                        USING dBASE III PLUS
COMMANDS                                       CREATE/MODIFY QUERY

Options           dBASE III PLUS provides menus for building the conditions in the
                  query file . The menu selections are Set Filter, Nest, Display, and
                  Exit .

Set Filter        A table appears with this menu which displays existing filter condi-
                  tions. You need to make an entry for each option in this menu . The
                  highlight automatically moves to the next option as you complete
                  entries.
                  The Field Name option offers a submenu of field names to choose
                  from.
                  The Operator option activates a list of operators specific to the data
                  type of the field specified in Field Name .
                  The Constant/Expression option is the only one in which you can
                  make an entry rather than select one from a list of fields or opera-
                  tors. If you want to specify fields from the submenu of field names
                  into the expression you are entering, press F10 . If you make your
                  own entry, the data type of the expression must match the field
                  name specified. That means you have to enclose character strings in
                  quotes, or include any functions necessary to convert data . Date
                  entries, however, are automatically converted, so you can enter
                  them directly in the format mm/dd/yy without using the CTOD()
                  function .
                  The Connect option links conditions . The operators linking condi-
                  tions together are .AND ., .OR., .AND . SNOT., and .OR . .NOT . You
                  pick the operator you want to use from a selection menu . At the
                  end of the last condition, select the No combination option .
                  The Line Number option lets you select one of the seven condi-
                  tions so you can edit it . You can change the field name, operator, or
                  expression for the selected line in the query table .
                   • To insert a new condition on the line at the current line num-
                     ber, press Ctrl-N .
                   • To delete the condition on the current line, press Ctrl-U .

Nest              Nesting allows you to determine the order in which conditions are
                  evaluated by adding or removing parentheses around conditions .

CREATE/MODIFY QUERY                                                    CHAPTER 5


           Start options add or remove a left parenthesis at the beginning of a
           line on the conditions table . After choosing Start, enter the line
           number.
           End options add or remove a right parenthesis after the
           Constant/Expression on the conditions table . After choosing End,
           enter the line number .

Display    This allows you to view individual records to see if you set the filter
           properly . It displays records which match the conditions set up in
           the query one at a time . You can view additional records, or view
           remaining fields of the same record, by pressing PgUp or PgDn .

           cally activates the qryy file .
           The Abandon option abandons the creation or modification of the

           ing a query file by pressing Esc.

CREATE/           CREATE/MODIFY REPORT is a full-screen, menu-driven command
                  used to create or change report format ( .frm) files .
MODIFY
REPORT

Syntax            CREATE/MODIFY REPORT G .frm filename > /?

Defaults          Unless you specify otherwise, report files are given the .frm exten-
                  sion . If a catalog is open and SET CATALOG is ON, the .frm file is
                  added to the catalog.

Usage             You use the CREATE REPORT command to create a report form
                  ( .frm) file, and the MODIFY REPORT command to modify an exist-
                  ing one . If you have a catalog open, you can enter the command
                  MODIFY REPORT ?. This command displays a list of .frm files asso-
                  ciated with the active database file, from which you can select .
                  The report form file specifies the basic arrangement of the report,
                  the location of fields in columns, the text for a report title, and
                  headings for columns . The report form file may specify fields from
                  one database file or fields from related database files . The REPORT
                  command is used to print reports using the report form file in
                  which fields are printed in table format under the respective col-
                  umns you specified .
                  You need to press 4J before you can make entries in the report
                  form menus, to change report settings, or before you specify the
                  headings and fields on the report . Title and column Heading
                  entries are made in a four-line entry area . Pressing Ctrl-End com-
                  pletes your entry .
                  A menu at the bottom of the screen displays the keys you can use
                  while creating or modifying a report . Press F1 Help to display this
                  menu or clear it from the screen .
                  Entries for report column and grouping expressions are made on
                  the entry lines provided within the menus . As your entries reach the
                  end of the line, the characters are scrolled horizontally to the left to
                  allow you to enter more text . You can use the - and -* keys to
                  move the cursor back and forth on the line, to review or edit your
                  entries .




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                 U5-73
CREATE/MODIFY REPORT                                                 CHAPTER 5


         To see the entire expression as you edit it, press Ctri-PgDn to display
         a full-length editing line at the bottom of the screen . You can use
         this zoom option to edit each report column expression . When you
         finish editing these lines, press Ctrl-PgUp to return to the editing
         line in the Groups or Columns Menus .
         While you're entering an expression, you can press F10 to display a
         list of field names from the database file in use or fields specified by
         the SET FIELDS TO command . You select a field by highlighting it
         on the field list and pressing 4J . The field automatically appears in
         the expression you're entering . You can use this feature as a short-
         cut to specifying fields, or as a reminder of the fields in your
         database file.
         After you've finished creating a report and have saved it, the

Options           The CREATE/MODIFY REPORT menu bar offers five choices :
                  Options, Groups, Columns, Locate, and Exit .

Options           The Page title option offers four lines in which to type a title for the
                  report . Pressing   at this option opens an editing screen for typing .
                  Pressing Ctrl-End closes the entry and returns back to the menu .
                  The Page width option determines the number of characters across
                  a page . The default value is 80 characters . The range of values
                  allowed is 1 to 500 .
                  The Left margin option determines the number of spaces the
                  report is offset on the left side of the page . You can specify an addi-
                  tional offset using the SET MARGIN command.




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                                   U5-75
CREATE/MODIFY REPORT                                                 CHAPTER 5


         The Right margin option determines the number of spaces the
         report is offset from the right side of the page .
         dBASE III PLUS checks the page width and the left and right mar-
         gin entries for consistency .
         The Lines per page option lets you put between 1 and 500 lines on
         a page before the page EJECTS . It does not reset the default page
         length on your printer .
         The Double space report option lets you choose between single- or
         double-spaced printing. The default value is NO, which creates a
         single-spaced report .
         The Page eject before printing option has a default of YES, which
         causes the printer to automatically eject a page before starting to
         print . If you change it to NO, the report starts printing wherever the
         paper is aligned in the printer .
         You can also suppress the page eject by including a NOEJECT when
         you issue the REPORT command to send the report to the screen or
         printer . This overrides a YES on the Options Menu .
         The Page eject after printing option has a default value of NO . You
         can eject the last page of the report after printing the report by
         changing the value to YES . This is equivalent to issuing EJECT after
         printing a report .



           NOTE
           If you want to print several short reports on one page, do
           not change the default of No for Page eject after printing .



         The Plain page option determines whether the page number, sys-
         tem date, and any heading defined with the HEADING option of
         the REPORT command are included on each page of the report .
         With the default value, NO, these pieces of information are included
         on each page . If the Plain page setting is YES, the title appears only
         on the first page, and no heading, page number, or date appears at
         all .



U5-76                                                    USING dBASE III PLUS
COMMANDS                                      CREATE/MODIFY REPORT

                  You can also activate the Plain page option when you issue the
                  REPORT command to output the report to the screen or printer . If
                  you include PLAIN with the REPORT command, it overrides a NO
                  set in the Options menu ; page numbers, dates, and titles are not
                  included in the report .

Groups            Entries in the Groups Menu are optional when creating a report .
                  However, if your database files are indexed, grouping records pro-
                  vides an additional level of detail in the report .
                  The Group on expression option lets you organize your report by
                  printing all records with the same value in a field or key expression
                  under the same group heading . This is particularly useful if you
                  want to create subtotals.
                  dBASE III PLUS starts a new group whenever it encounters a new
                  value . Therefore, make sure that you INDEX or SORT the file on
                  the same field or expression that you group records in the report .
                  For example, you can group the report on the field Travelcode in
                  Travel .dbf. Then, if you index the file by Travelcode, you can
                  create a report listing all people who signed up for the same trip.
                  You specify the fields you want to print under each group in the
                  Contents option in the Columns Menu .
                  The Group heading option specifies the text printed on the report
                  with each group expression (see Figure 5-5) . For example, if the
                  heading is "Travel Code," the report will print Travel Code
                  followed by the name of the trip before it lists the people who are
                  going on the trip .
                  The Summary report only option determines whether all the
                  records for each group are displayed, or only their totals . The
                  default value, NO, displays all contents and totals .
                  The Page eject after group option determines whether each group
                  is printed immediately after the previous one, or is printed on a sep-
                  arate sheet of paper . The default value, NO, keeps the groups
                  together on a page .




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                 U5-77
CREATE/MODIFY REPORT                                                   CHAPTER 5


          The Sub-group on expression option lets you further categorize
          groups of records in a report . For example, if the same travel pack-
          age is repeated on different dates, you could INDEX the file on the
          Travelcode and Departure fields . Then, you could group the report
          by Travelcode, and specify the Departure date as a sub-group . The
          report will list in a sub-group all the people who have the same
          departure date .
          The Sub-group heading option specifies the text introduction to the
          sub-group, for example, the subgroup heading of "Departure Date"
          would be displayed prior to the sub-group expression .

Columns   You make entries in the Columns Menu to specify the fields on the
          report . A report can have up to 24 columns.
          To delete an existing column, press Ctrl-U . To insert a new column,
          press Ctrl-N .
          The Contents option specifies what goes in each column . This can
          be a field name or an expression .
          If the contents is a field name, press iJ to access the option, then
          press F10 to activate a list of field names from which to choose . To
          select a field, highlight it and press i-J . Press -* or E- to return to
          the main menu .
          If the contents is an expression, type it in the entry area .
          The Heading option identifies the contents of each column . You
          can enter up to four lines with up to 65 characters on each line . To
          begin making an entry, you need to press 4 .J to open an entry area
          in which to create the column heading . Pressing Ctrl-End closes the
          entry area returning to the menu .
          The Width option determines the size of the column . It automati-
          cally defaults to the field, expression, or heading size, whichever is
          larger (up to a maximum default of 30) . You can increase or
          decrease this size . If the column is narrower than the
          field/expression or heading you entered, both will wrap when they
          are displayed .
          The Decimal places option is for numeric values . It defaults to the
          number of decimal places specified in the file structure . If you
          decrease the size, the number is rounded .

                  The Total this column option is for numeric values, and allows you

                  report.

Locate            When you open the Locate Menu, a list of all the fields or expres-

CREATE/    CREATE/MODIFY SCREEN is a full-screen, menu-driven command
           you can use to create custom screen forms . It generates both a
MODIFY     screen ( .scr) and a format ( .fmt) file . The CREATE/MODIFY
SCREEN     SCREEN command provides "screen painter" functions allowing
           you to change the way fields appear on your screen when you use
           the APPEND and EDIT commands . While you are creating the cus-
           tom screen form with this command, you can also modify the struc-
           ture of the database file .

Syntax     CREATE/MODIFY SCREEN < .scr filename > /?

Defaults   Unless you specify otherwise, CREATE/MODIFY SCREEN creates or
           modifies a screen format file with the .scr file extension . When you
           save a screen format file, a format file with the .fmt file extension is
           created . If a catalog is open, and SET CATALOG is ON, the screen
           ( .scr) file and format ( .fmt) file are added to the catalog .

Usage      You use the CREATE SCREEN command to create a new screen
           format file . You use MODIFY SCREEN < filename > /? to alter an
           existing screen format file .
           If a catalog is open, you can type MODIFY SCREEN ? to display a
           list of screen ( .scr) files associated with the active database file .
           When you exit the Screen Menu with the Save option,
           dBASE III PLUS automatically generates a format ( .fmt) file with
           the same name as the .scr file and activates the format file it gener-
           ates . To deactivate an open format ( .fmt) file, type SET FORMAT
           TO 4J or open another format file .

                       WARNING

                       • You specify a format ( .fmt) file with the SET FORMAT TO

          A field width must be specified for numeric and character fields .
          This is the maximum number of digits or characters you intend to
          enter in the field . Character fields may be up to 254 characters
          long; numeric fields may be up to 19 digits including the sign and a
          decimal point .
          Date, Logical, and Memo fields all have predefined widths . Date
          fields are always 8 characters and logical fields are always 1 charac-
          ter. Memo fields are automatically assigned a length of 10 in the
          database file, although the entry in a memo field may be up to 5,000
          characters, or larger, depending on the word processor used . Data
          entered in memo fields is not stored in the database ( .dbf) file but
          in an associated memo (.dbt) text file .
          You can define a record having up to 128 fields. The maximum size
          of a record is 4,000 bytes . Each character position in a field takes
          up one byte. Memo fields use 10 bytes, even though the memo data
          is not actually stored in the database file . The 10 bytes identify the
          location of memo field entries in the memo file .
          Instructions and error messages appear at the bottom of the screen
          as you create the database file . In addition, a cursor navigation
          menu appears at the top of the screen indicating the operations you
          can perform and the keys you can use . You can make the menu
          appear or disappear from the screen by pressing F1 .
          Below the menu, the entries for each field appear . Each field
          appears on a separate line containing the field name, the data type,
          the width, and the number of decimal digits (for a numeric field) . A
          highlight appears on the current field, and a blinking cursor
          appears on the current entry column .
          The arrow keys move the cursor to any field. When the fields take
          up more than a single screen, you can use the PgUp and PgDn keys
          to scroll forward or backward through the fields . When you create a
          new field, the cursor cannot be advanced beyond an incomplete
          field (or a field definition that is invalid), but can be moved back-
          ward to previous fields .

COMMANDS               CREATE < newfile > /MODIFY STRUCTURE
                  If you forget to include a field, and want to insert it, position the
                  cursor where you want to insert the field and press Ctrl-N . The
                  order in which you enter data in fields is determined by the field
                  position in the database file, using the default data entry form
                  dBASE III PLUS provides, or by the position of fields on a custom
                  entry form created with CREATE/MODIFY SCREEN .
                  To delete a field, position the cursor on the appropriate field and
                  press Ctri-U . If at any point you want to abandon the file you are
                  creating, press Esc .
                  When you're finished creating the database file structure, press
                  Ctrl-End or press    at the beginning of a new field. You will see a
                  prompt asking you to confirm that you want to save the file . Press
                  4J to save the file, or press any other key to resume . If you do save
                  the file, you will next be asked whether you want to begin inputting
                  records .

MODIFY            This command is used to modify the structure of an existing
STRUCTURE         database file . You can use this command to add new fields, delete
                  fields, or change a field's name, data type, or width . When you're
                  finished making changes, you save the new structure by pressing
                  Ctrl-End .
                  You can move through the displayed field name, width, type, and
                  decimal columns using the      and -+ keys, or you can press Ctrl-~-
                  and Ctrl-- to move the highlight from field to field .
                  You can insert new fields using the MODIFY STRUCTURE
                  command . Move the highlight to the field in the structure where
                  you want to insert a field and press Ctrl-N . The field will be inserted
                  in front of the highlighted field in the database file structure .
                  Remember that the order in which you enter data in fields is deter-
                  mined by the position of fields in the database file using the default
                  data entry form dBASE III PLUS provides, or by the position of
                  fields on a custom entry form created with CREATE/MODIFY
                  SCREEN .

                  dBASE III PLUS will successfully convert data for a number of field
                  type conversions . However, if you are changing field types, keep a
                  backup copy of your original file, and check your new files to make
                  sure the data has converted correctly .
                  If you convert numeric fields to character fields, numbers from the
                  numeric fields will be converted to character strings . If you convert
                  a character field to a numeric field, numeric characters in each
                  record will be converted to digits until dBASE III PLUS encounters
                  the first non-numeric character in each field . If the first character
                  in a character field is a letter, the converted numeric field will be
                  blank .
                  You can also convert logical fields to character fields, or vice versa .
                  You cannot convert logical fields to numeric fields . You can also
                  convert character strings which are formatted as a date (for exam-
                  ple, mm/dd/yy or mm-dd-yy) to a date field, or convert date fields
                  to character fields .

                  If you modify fields in a database file which are used in an index file
                  key expression, you'll have to re-create the index file . If an index
                  file is open when you modify a database file, it will automatically be
                  closed when you save your changes to the database file .

CREATE/    CREATE/MODIFY VIEW is a full-screen, menu-driven command
           that creates a file to link one or more related database files and
MODIFY     their ancillary files .
VIEW

Syntax     CREATE/MODIFY VIEW < .vue filename > /?

Defaults   Unless otherwise specified, dBASE III PLUS creates a view file with
           the .vue file extension . If a catalog is open, and SET CATALOG is
           ON, the .vue file is added to the catalog .

Usage      You use the CREATE VIEW command to create a new view file .
           You use the MODIFY VIF~W command to alter an existing view file .
           If you want to alter an existing view file from the current catalog,
           but you do not remember its name, type MODIFY VIEW ? This dis-
           plays a list of view files in the open catalog . If you want to create a
           view file that is based on the current database files in use and a
           SET RELATION, use the CREATE VIEW FROM ENVIRONMENT
           command.
           CREATE/MODIFY VIEW creates or modifies a view ( .vue) file
           which defines the database files, index files, and the fields in a view,
           and sets up a relation between files (see SET RELATION) . It also
           allows you to select a format file for display and entry of records,
           and to specify a filter condition to select records from the related
           database files you'll be able to see . When you want to use the rela-
           tion and file setup in the view file again, issue the SET VIEW TO
           command . This command sets up the database and related files
           defined in the view file .
           When you exit CREATE/MODIFY VIEW with the Save option,
           dBASE III PLUS automatically activates the new .vue file . To deacti-
           vate a .vue file, type CLOSE DATABASES. This closes all open .dbf,
           .ndx, and .fmt files. However, it does not close any open .cat file.
           All .vue files contain the following elements :
            • Database and associated index files and the work area selections
               for each of these files
            • Relations between the files (if more than one database file is
               selected)
            • Currently selected work area

                  Additionally, they can contain the following optional elements :
                   • Selected fields from each database file ; with the CREATE/
                     MODIFY VIEW command, these are set from the Set Fields
                     Menu . With CREATE VIEW FROM ENVIRONMENT, these are
                     set with the SET FIELDS TO command .
                   • A format ( .fmt) file
                   • A filter condition

Relate            When you open the Relate Menu, all of the filenames selected in the
                  Set Up Menu appear .

Options           The Filter option lets you specify a condition which must be met
                  for any particular record to be included when the view file is used .
                  See SET FILTER TO for details . The entry area scrolls horizontally,
                  letting you enter an expression of up to 254 characters .
                  An important function of the Filter option is that it lets you set up a
                  filter condition on fields other than those linking the database files .
                  For example, two files, Travel and Clients, are linked by a common
                  field, Lastname . You could set up a filter which includes only the
                  fields for a Travelcode of CI10, by specifying the condition
                  Travelcode = 'CI10' . If you want to specify a condition containing
                  a field which is not in the current work area, you can specify the
                  alias of the work area with the field, for example :

                               clients - > state = 'CA'

                  Refer to the SELECT command for a description of work areas and
                  ALIAS names .
                  Choosing the Format option displays a list of format ( .fmt) files in
                  the open catalog, or on the default drive if no catalog is open . The
                  format file you choose will always be in effect when you open the
                  view file with the SET VIEW TO command .
                  If you want to create a .fmt file for a .vue file, save the .vue file and
                  use CREATE SCREEN or MODIFY COMMAND to design the custom
                  screen format. The format file should contain only fields that are
                  accessible in the view . You can then return to the Format option of
                  MODIFY VIEW and choose the new .fmt file from the menu list .

Exit              The Save option stores the newly created .vue file or saves changes
                  made to an existing one . This automatically activates the .vue file .
                  The Abandon option discards a newly created .vue file, or disre-
                  gards changes made to an existing one . This is equivalent to press-
                  ing Esc .

Tips              With the Files value set to 20 in Config .sys, you can have 15 files
                  open . When you open a .vue file, make sure that you have enough
                  room to open the files stored in the view : .dbf files, any associated
                  .ndx and .fmt files, as well as space for the .vue file . The view file is
                  only open as long as it takes to set up the other files .

DELETE     DELETE marks records in the active database file for deletion .

Syntax     DELETE [ < scope > ] [WHILE < condition > ]
           [FOR < condition > ]

Defaults   Unless otherwise specified by the scope or the WHILE or FOR
           clause, only the current record is marked for deletion .

Usage      With DISPLAY and LIST, records marked for deletion are indicated
           by an asterisk (*) in the first position of the record . You can
           unmark records already marked for deletion with RECALL .
           With full-screen commands such as BROWSE or EDIT, records
           marked for deletion are indicated by Del on the status bar . In this
           mode, Ctrl-U both deletes and reinstates records .

Record     DELETE with no parameters does not reposition the record pointer .
           Therefore, if you're at the end of the file, as after LIST or DISPLAY
Pointer    ALL, issuing DELETE has no effect .

Examples   To mark only the first record in the Clients database for deletion :

             • USE Clients
             • DELETE
                    1 record deleted


           To mark record 6 for deletion :

             • DELETE RECORD 6
                   1 record deleted

             . RECALL ALL
                   2 records recalled


See Also   DELETED(), PACK, RECALL, SET DELETED ON

DIR               DIR displays the filenames, number of records, date of last update,
                  and file size (in bytes) for each database file on the indicated disk
                  drive . It is also possible to display the names of other types of files .
                  DIR also shows the number of filenames displayed, the total num-

                  remaining on the disk .

Syntax            DIR [ < drive : > ] [ < path > ] [ < skeleton > ]

                  An alternate syntax is :

                  DISPLAY/LIST FILES [LIKE < skeleton > ] [TO PRINT]

                  default drive and directory is displayed .

Usage             The directory will not reflect changes after records are added to or
                  eliminated from a database file until the file is closed .
                  DISPLAY/LIST FILES are an alternative for DIR, except that they
                  display files only in the current directory.

Special Cases     If Config .sys is set to FILES = 20 and 15 files are open (including
                  format files, program files, etc .), typing DIR displays not readable
                  in the # records column .

                       • DIR

                       • DIR * .NDX

                       • DIR ??D?? .

DISPLAY           DISPLAY is used to view the contents of a database file .

Syntax            DISPLAY [ < scope > ] [[FIELDS] < expression list > ]
                  [WHILE < condition > ] [FOR < condition > ] [OFF] [TO PRINT]

Defaults          The current record is displayed, unless otherwise specified by the
                  scope or WHILE or FOR clause .
                  All fields are displayed unless otherwise specified .
                  The record number is displayed unless the OFF option is included .

Usage             If more than 20 records are displayed, DISPLAY pauses after every
                  20 lines . dBASE III PLUS then prompts Press any key to
                  continue . . .
                  The contents of memo fields are not displayed unless explicitly
                  named in the FIELDS expression list . Instead, the field name
                  appears above the word Memo in the display . If memo fields are
                  named in the expression list, their contents are displayed in
                  50-character wide columns . Use the SET MEMOWIDTH command
                  to change this default display width .
                  At the end of the file (EOF() is .T .), DISPLAY shows headings only,
                  as there are no remaining records to display .
                  When a record is DISPLAYed that is greater than 80 characters, the
                  contents wrap around to the next line and may break up a field
                  onto two or more lines .

Special Cases     Each column has a heading . If the displayed item is the result of an
                  expression involving a field (for example Cost/25), the column
                  heading is the same as the expression .
                  The heading appears as you typed it . To receive all capital letters,
                  type DISPLAY FIELD 1 . For upper and lower case headings, type
                  DISPLAY Fieldl .

U5-110                                                       USING dBASE III PLUS
COMMANDS                                                                            DO

DO                DO causes a dBASE III PLUS command file or procedure to be exe-
                  cuted . It may also pass parameters to the named program .

Syntax            DO < filename > [WITH < parameter list > ]

Defaults          The filename must include the drive designator if the file is not on
                  the default drive, unless a path is set . A .prg extension is assumed
                  unless otherwise specified .

Usage             Each DO < filename > counts as an open file . The total number of
                  open files (database files, index files, format files, command files,
                  and so on) cannot be more than 15 (FILES = 20) . If you are using a
                  procedure file, only the one named with SET PROCEDURE TO
                   < filename > counts as an open file .
                  When the program called by DO is complete, control returns to the
                  calling program, or to the keyboard if the DO was issued from the
                  dot prompt .
                  Memory variables created in called programs must be declared
                  PUBLIC if they're used after the called program terminates . All
                  PRIVATE memory variables created within programs are released
                  once the program terminates .

Options           The WITH option allows passing of parameters to the subroutine .
                  The parameter list can contain any valid dBASE III PLUS expres-
                  sions . To specify a field name to take precedence over a memory
                  variable with the same name, specify the alias name of the work
                  area in which the database file is open .

Examples          Assume that you have a program named Taxes .prg which is located
                  on drive B, while the default drive is A . To execute the program,
                  type :
                       DO B :Taxes

U5-112                                                                    USING      dBASE   III   PLUS
COMMANDS                                                                 DO CASE
DO CASE           DO CASE is a structured programming command that selects only
                  one course of action from a set of alternatives .

Syntax            DO CASE
                     CASE < condition >
                         • commands >
                     [CASE < condition > ]
                         • commands >
                     [OTHERWISE]
                         • commands >
                  ENDCASE

Usage             ENDCASE terminates the DO CASE structure . Command pairs such
                  as DO CASE . . . ENDCASE, IF . . . ENDIF, and DO WHILE . . . ENDDO
                  must be properly nested within DO CASE . Nested DO CASES are
                  permitted .
                  CASE < condition > sets up a conditional statement for evaluation .
                  It is a logical expression such as A = B or numvar <11 . When
                   < condition > evaluates to logical True, all subsequent commands
                  are carried out until any one of the following commands is reached :
                  another CASE, OTHERWISE, or ENDCASE .
                  After one True CASE is found and its associated commands
                  processed, no further CASE statements are evaluated .
                  dBASE III PLUS skips immediately to the first command after
                  ENDCASE . If no CASE statements evaluate to True, and there is no
                  OTHERWISE statement, the program processes the first command
                  following ENDCASE . OTHERWISE causes the program to take an
                  alternative path of action when all CASE statements evaluate to
                  False .

Tips              In instances where only one of many conditions will evaluate to
                  True, or where only the first True instance is to be processed, the
                  DO CASE command is preferable to the IF command .
                  The CASE construct is often used when there are a small number of
                  exceptions to a condition . The CASE < condition > statements can
                  represent the exceptions, and the OTHERWISE statement the more
                  common situation .

See Also          DO, DO WHILE, IF, MODIFY COMMAND



USING dBASE III PLUS                                                              U5-113
DO WHILE                                                           CHAPTER 5


DO WHILE   DO WHILE is a structured programming command that allows
           command statements between it and its associated ENDDO to be
           repeated as long as the specified condition is True .

Syntax     DO WHILE < condition >
               • commands >
               [EXIT]
               • commands >
               [LOOP]
               • commands >
           ENDDO

Usage      ENDDO must terminate a DO WHILE structure .
           EXIT transfers control from within a DO WHILE . . . ENDDO loop to
           the command immediately following the ENDDO .
           LOOP returns control to the beginning of a DO WHILE . . . ENDDO
           program structure . LOOP prevents the execution of the remaining
           commands in the DO WHILE construct .
                                                          ..
           Any structured commands within a DO WHILE . ENDDO structure
           must be properly nested . Nested DO WHILES are permitted .
           Comments entered following ENDDO on the same line are ignored .
           DO WHILE < condition > opens a structured procedure that pro-
           cesses subsequent commands only while the condition evaluates to
           True, for example, .NOT. EOF() .AND . mvarl = 11 .
           If < condition > evaluates to a logical True, all subsequent com-
           mands are carried out until an ENDDO, LOOP, or EXIT is encoun-
           tered . ENDDO and LOOP return control to the DO WHILE com-
           mand for another evaluation of < condition > . EXIT passes control
           to the statement following the ENDDO .
           If the condition evaluates to a logical False, dBASE III PLUS skips
           all commands between DO WHILE and ENDDO and goes to the
           command following ENDDO .




U5-114                                                  USING dBASE III PLUS
COMMANDS                                                                    DO WHILE
Programming       You can use macros in the conditional portion of a DO WHILE loop
                  only if the value of the variable in the macro does not change, as
Notes             the DO WHILE statement is parsed only the first time through the
                  loop . After the first time, the DO WHILE statement is executed from
                  memory . Also, macro substitution must be within the lowest nested
                  level of a program .

Examples          The first example shows how to correctly use a macro in the condi-
                  tional portion of a DO WHILE loop executing in a dBASE program
                  file :

                       FIND Keegan
                       DO WHILE &condition .AND . SNOT . EOFO
                            The value of condition never changes
                             ? TRIM(Fi rstname), Lastname
                          SKIP
                       ENDDO
                       USE
                       RETURN

EDIT                                                                  CHAPTER 5


EDIT       EDIT is a full-screen command used to alter the contents of a
           record in the active database file .

Syntax     EDIT [ < scope > ] [FIELDS < list > ] [WHILE < condition > ]
           [FOR < condition > ]

Defaults   If EDIT is used without parameters, the current record is EDITed .

Usage      EDIT uses the standard full-screen cursor control keys . The arrow
           keys move the cursor within a record . PgUp backs up to the previ-
           ous record . PgDn advances to the next record . To exit and save all
           changes, press Ctrl-End . Press Esc to save changes to all but the cur-
           rent record .
           To EDIT a memo field, enter Ctrl-PgDn when the cursor is
           positioned at the beginning of the field . The control key functions
           are the same as for MODIFY COMMAND . To exit from this mode,
           enter Ctrl-End to save changes or Esc to exit and abandon changes
           to the current record .
           EDIT and CHANGE are identical commands

Example    To EDIT the 21st record in the Clients database file :

             • USE Clients
             • EDIT RECORD 21

EJECT                                                                  CHAPTER 5


EJECT      EJECT causes the printer to advance the paper to the top of the
           next page .

Syntax     EJECT

Usage      EJECT issues a form feed (ASCII character value of 12) to the
           printer . For proper printer operation, the paper must initially be set
           to the top-of-form . Refer to your printer manual for instructions on
           how to set top-of-form .
           Issuing an EJECT when the printer is either not connected or not
           turned on may "lock" the computer . Connecting and turning on the
           printer should "unlock" it . Otherwise, the computer must be
           restarted, which can result in data loss . Consult your computer
           operating manual for instructions .
           EJECT resets PROW() and PCOL() to zero .

See Also   PCOL(), PROW(), SET DEVICE, SET PRINT

EXPORT                                                                  CHAPTER 5


EXPORT     EXPORT exports the open dBASE III PLUS database file to a file
           format useable by pfs :File . The records are exported in an indexed
           order if an index file is in use . A screen form will also be exported
           if a format file is in use .

Syntax     EXPORT TO < filename > [TYPE] PFS

Defaults   The file has the same name as the dBASE III PLUS database ( .dbf)
           file from which it was made . pfs :File forms normally do not have a
           file extension, however, you can provide one .

Usage      This command acts on an active database file and its ancillary files,
           merging them into a single pfs :File form . The original
           dBASE III PLUS files remain intact after an EXPORT .
           The format of the fields in the newly created file depends on
           whether a format file is engaged when you EXPORT . If no format
           (.fmt) file is SET, EXPORT uses the dBASE III PLUS default entry
           format provided for commands such as APPEND and EDIT .
           If the dBASE III PLUS database file was previously created with
           IMPORT, it has an associated format ( .fmt) file . If a format file is
           selected using the SET FORMAT TO command, EXPORT uses that
           form. If the database file has several format ( .fmt) files, EXPORT
           uses whichever form is open .
           When you EXPORT a format file, check that it does not contain
           more than 200 @a commands . Also, the form should not specify
           more than 21 rows . The rows specified on your form must be
           between row 0 and row 20 .
           If a TO file already exists and SET SAFETY is ON, you are warned
           about overwriting . If SET SAFETY is OFF, the existing PFS file is
           overwritten automatically, even if you have an unacceptable format
           file .

                       larger than your other software can accept . Although these
                       fields are exported, they may be cut short by the other program .
                       Note the limitations of other programs before creating files for
                       them with EXPORT .

                       • SET FORMAT TO Tours

FIND            FIND searches an indexed database file for the first record with an
                index key that matches the specified character string or number .
                FIND conducts a very rapid record search .

Syntax          FIND < character string > / < n >

Tips            SEEK has a similar function but, unlike FIND, it can search for an
                expression .
                LOCATE also has a similar function but doesn't require an indexed
                file .

Record          If the specified character string or number is not found, the mes-
                sage No Find, displays on the screen . SET TALK OFF suppresses
Pointer         this message . The record pointer moves to the end of the file, EOF()
                is True, and FOUND() will return False .

Special Cases   FIND works without delimiters if the character string for which you
                are searching does not contain leading blanks and does not begin
                with a character normally used as a delimiter . If there are leading
                blanks, the specified string must include the exact number of lead-
                ing blanks and be enclosed in single or double quotation marks, or
                square brackets . If a character string begins with a delimiter charac-
                ter, for example, 'two, you need to specify FIND with delimiters,
                and choose a different delimiter than that in a character string .
                When searching for the contents of a character memory variable,
                the variable must be used with the & (Macro) function . If the mem-
                ory variable contains leading blanks, you must enclose the function
                in quotation marks : "& < memvar > ".

IF                                                                  CHAPTER 5


IF         IF is a structured programming command that enables conditional
           processing of commands . It must terminate with ENDIF.

Syntax     IF < condition >
              < commands >
           [ELSE]
              < commands >
           ENDIF
                                                    .
Usage      Any structured commands within an IF . . ENDIF structure must be
           properly nested . Nested IFs are permissible .
           The space following ENDIF on a line may be used for comments .
           IF < condition > sets up a conditional statement which is a logical
           expression such as (A = B or Numvar <11) for evaluation . If
            < condition > evaluates to logical True, all subsequent commands
           are carried out until an ELSE, or the ENDIF if no ELSE exists, is
           reached . dBASE III PLUS then executes the first command after
           ENDIF.
           If < condition > evaluates to logical False, dBASE III PLUS goes
           directly to the ELSE or ENDIF, whichever it encounters first . ELSE
           causes all subsequent commands to be carried out until ENDIF is
           reached .
           If there are multiple IFs in a command structure, ELSE refers to
           the IF immediately preceding it .

See Also   DO CASE, IIF()

COMMANDS                                                                     IMPORT

IMPORT            IMPORT creates dBASE III PLUS files from pfs :File forms .

Syntax            IMPORT FROM < filename > [TYPE] PFS

Defaults          The filename must include the file extension if one exists, although
                  files imported from pfs :File do not usually have an extension . The
                  newly created dBASE III PLUS files are given the same name as the
                  pfs:File form . If a catalog is open, the new file is added to the cata-
                  log . Records created in the new database file are limited to a maxi-
                  mum of 4,000 bytes .
                  IMPORT will locate a file on a drive or directory specified with a
                  dBASE path (SET PATH TO command) . If no drive or path is speci-
                  fied, dBASE III PLUS assumes that the file to be imported is on the
                  default drive and directory.

Usage             To make sure that you import data correctly, check your pfs :File
                  form before using the IMPORT command for the following
                  conditions :
                   •   128 data items per form . You can have up to 128 fields in a
                       record. Notice, however, that headings and comments in your
                       pfs:File form are also converted to fields .
                   • 254 characters per data item . 254 is the maximum length for
                     character fields in dBASE III PLUS .
                  IMPORT automatically separates the IMPORTed file into several
                  files understood by dBASE III PLUS : a database (.dbf), format (.fmt),
                  and a view ( .vue) file. All have the same filename, and are assigned
                  default file extensions by dBASE III PLUS .
                  dBASE III PLUS creates the view file by internally performing the
                  equivalent of the following commands at the end of its IMPORT
                  procedure :
                  USE < filename >
                  SET FORMAT TO < .fmt filename >
                  CREATE VIEW < .vue filename > FROM ENVIRONMENT




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                U5-129
IMPORT                                                                   CHAPTER 5


           By performing an internal CREATE VIEW FROM ENVIRONMENT
           command, dBASE III PLUS creates a view ( .vue) file that contains
           both the .dbf file and the .fmt file . All files are entered in the cata-
           log, if one is open .
           In future sessions, open the file with either USE or SET VIEW TO .
           If you use SET VIEW, both the database file and the format file are
           opened . USE only opens the database file ; to use the format file, you
           must also specify the SET FORMAT TO command .
           When IMPORT creates a format file, it may create       statements
           with column references outside the range of 0 to 79 . If so, you need
           to use MODIFY COMMAND or another word processor to modify
           the file. If you use IMPORT to overwrite an existing database ( .dbf)
           file, answer Yes to all three overwrite prompts that appear on your
           screen . This ensures that the created database, format, and view
           files can still be used together .

Examples   Assume you have pfs :File data in a file named Agents . To create
           dBASE III PLUS files from it, you would type :

              . IMPORT FROM Agents TYPE PFS
           The IMPORT command creates the necessary files and puts them in
           use . To display information about the imported file use the

U5-130                                                        USING dBASE III PLUS
COMMANDS                                                                      INDEX

INDEX             The INDEX command creates a file in which index keys from an
                  associated database file are ordered alphabetically, chronologically,
                  or numerically . The index file contains the index key values and the
                  corresponding record number for each record in the database file .

Syntax            INDEX [ON < key expression > TO < filename > [UNIQUE]]

Defaults          Unless otherwise specified as part of the filename, the default drive
                  and an .ndx extension are assumed .
                  If you only type INDEX .-', dBASE III PLUS prompts for the index
                  expression and the index filename .
                  When SET SAFETY is ON (the default), dBASE III PLUS displays a
                  warning prompt before overwriting an index file with the same
                  name as the new index file .

Usage             You specify an index key expression to order the records of an asso-
                  ciated database file . INDEXing always occurs in ascending order .
                  The database file records are not physically rearranged by the
                  INDEX operation . Instead, the order is maintained by the index
                  ( .ndx) file, which must then be used with the database file for the
                  records to appear in the desired order .
                  The index key expression may be a single field or any valid dBASE
                  expression, however, it may not contain logical or memo fields . The
                  maximum length of the index key expression is 220 characters . The
                  maximum length of the index key, the length of the result of the
                  evaluated index key expression, is 100 characters .
                  The data type of the index key expression determines whether
                  records will be ordered chronologically (by date), alphabetically
                  (character strings), or numerically .




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                              U5-131
INDEX                                                                  CHAPTER 5


          When the index key expression includes several fields, they must all
          be converted in the expression to the same data type . Place the
          most important field first and then convert the remaining fields to
          create an expression that matches the data type of the first field .
          You can also use dBASE functions to convert your fields to the cor-
          rect type . Some of the functions most commonly used in creating
          index key expressions are STR(), CTOD(), DTOC(), YEAR(),
          MONTH(), DAY() and VAL() .
          The index file contains the index key values (the key expression
          evaluated) and the corresponding record number for each record in
          the database file . The index file maintains the order of records in a
          database file as long as the index file is open . Up to seven index file
          database files can be open at one time, however, the first one in a
          list controls the order in which records will appear (unless you use
          the SET ORDER TO command) .

Options   The UNIQUE option is the same as issuing SET UNIQUE ON before
          an INDEX . When several records have the same value on the key
          field, only the first record that dBASE III PLUS encounters with
          that value is included in the .ndx file .
          Whenever you REINDEX an .ndx file that was created with
          UNIQUE, the file retains its UNIQUE status, regardless of whether
          SET UNIQUE is ON or OFF .

Tips      You can specify index expressions that convert field types . For
          example, if you wanted to INDEX a date field chronologically and
          have the last names in alphabetical order for each date, you could
          create the following expression :
          INDEX ON STR(YEAR( < date > ),4) + STR(MONTH( < date > ),2)
          + STR(DAY( < date > ),2) + Last name TO < index filename >
          In this example, the date field is first converted to a numeric type
          using the YEAR(), MONTH(), and DAY() functions . Next, the
          numeric data is converted to character type data with the STR()
          function . Because Lastname is a character type field, the index key
          is also of character field type .




U5-132                                                     USING dBASE III PLUS
COMMANDS                                                                         INDEX

U5-134                                                    USING dBASE III PLUS
COMMANDS                                                                     INPUT

INPUT             INPUT is primarily used in dBASE programs to prompt a user to
                  enter an expression from the keyboard . Data entry is terminated by
                  a ~.

Syntax            INPUT [ < prompt > ] TO   < memvar >

Usage             The prompt you specify is a character expression . If the prompt is a
                  character string rather than a character memory variable, the
                  prompt must be delimited by single quotes ('), double quotes ("), or
                  square brackets([ ]) .
                  If a memory variable is used as a prompt, it must have been defined
                  previously, and must not be enclosed in quotes .
                  Any valid dBASE III PLUS expression can be entered in response to
                  the INPUT command. The type of expression entered determines
                  the type of memory variable created . For instance, if you enter a
                  number in response, a numeric memory variable is created .
                  If an invalid expression is entered in response to the INPUT com-
                  mand, an error message appears .
                  You must enter a response followed by ±-J. If you press 4J without
                  first making an entry, the prompt is redisplayed .

Programming       If it is important that the response be character type data, use
                  ACCEPT, WAIT, or . . . GET with the PICTURE option . ACCEPT
Notes             assumes that all user response is character and doesn't require
                  delimiters .
                  If you use an INPUT command that requires a date response,
                  include instructions in the prompt as to how the date should be
                  entered. Entry of the CTOD() function or other processing of the
                  entry is required when typing in date information .

U5-136                                                           USING dBASE III PLUS
COMMANDS                                                                        INSERT

INSERT            INSERT adds a single new record to the database file at the current
                  record location .

Syntax            INSERT [BLANK] [BEFORE]

Usage             INSERT displays the new record for full-screen data entry . Data
                  may be entered into this record only . The new record is inserted
                  immediately after the current record. For instance, if the current
                  record is number 5, INSERT creates a new record 6 ; the old record
                  6 becomes record 7, and so on .
                  In two instances, INSERT works like APPEND : if the file is indexed,
                  the record is placed at the end of the file ; and if a record is inserted
                  at the end of a file, it adds multiple records, one at a time .
                  Enter data into a memo field by placing the cursor on it (labeled
                  memo on the screen) and pressing Ctrl-PgDn . To exit the memo
                  field, press Ctrl-End to save, or Esc to exit without saving changes .
                  While editing the memo field, the control keys are the same as
                  those used with MODIFY COMMAND . Press F1 to toggle on and off
                  the menu displaying the keys you can use .
                  Arrow keys move the cursor within a record . Esc abandons the pro-
                  cess without inserting a new record, displaying the message Record
                  is not inserted . Ctrl-End terminates the process and completes the
                  record insertion .

Options           The BEFORE clause inserts a new record just before the current
                  record. For instance, if the current record is number 5, INSERT
                  BEFORE creates a new record 5 ; the old record 5 becomes record
                  6, and so on .
                  If BLANK is included, a new record is INSERTed, but full-screen
                  mode is not entered . Data may be added later using one of the edit-
                  ing commands .

Tip               To copy contents of the preceding record to the INSERTed record,
                  use SET CARRY ON .




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                U5-137
INSERT                                                               CHAPTER 5



Example    The Clients database file from the Sample Programs and Utilities
           disk is used for the following example .
           To insert a new record immediately before record 4 (that is, to cre-
           ate a new record 4), type the following :

             • SET STATUS ON
             . USE Clients
                 G04
                 INSERT BEFORE

U5-138                                                      USING dBASE III PLUS
COMMANDS                                                                            JOIN

JOIN              JOIN creates a new database file by merging specified records and
                  fields from two open database files .

Syntax            JOIN WITH < alias > TO < filename > FOR < condition >
                  [FIELDS < field list > ]

Defaults          The TO filename must include the drive and directory location if
                  the file is not in the current directory . The file extension .dbf is
                  assumed unless otherwise specified .

Usage             When JOINing an active file with an open file from an unselected
                  work area, the second file is identified by its alias name . This may
                  be the same as its filename .
                  The field list may consist of any type of field from both files except
                  memo fields . If you try to join memo fields, you will get the mes-
                  sage Operation with memo field invalid .
                  If no field list is specified, field assignments are made from the
                  active file first . Then, fields are assigned from the second file until
                  the 128-field limit is reached . Duplicate field names do not appear
                  in the new file .
                  JOIN updates a catalog if open and SET CATALOG is ON .

Record            The record pointer is set to the first record in the active file .
                  Each record in the second file is evaluated to see if it matches the
Pointer           FOR < condition > . If the specified condition is True, a new record
                  is added to the new file . When all records in the second file are
                  scanned, the record pointer in the active file advances one record,
                  and the process is repeated . This continues until all records in the
                  active file are processed . This operation can take a long time for
                  large files .

Tips              Do not use the single letters A through J or M as database file-
                  names, because they are reserved for ALIAS names . For example,
                  AA is a valid database filename whereas A is not .




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                 U5-139
JOIN                                                                         CHAPTER 5


                Make sure you have enough room when JOINing two files . It is pos-
                sible for two database files to be JOINed such that the new file
                exceeds the available disk space . It is possible for the new JOINed
                file to become quite large if the specified condition is not chosen
                carefully . For example, if two 1,000-record files were JOINed and
                the specified condition was always True, one million records would
                be created .

Special Cases   If both files have a field name in common and you want to specify a
                field from the unselected file, specify the field in the following form :
                alias- > field name . Fields which are specified using the SET FIELDS
                TO command may also be used . Use only the field name to specify a
                field in the active database file .

Examples        You can combine the Travel .dbf database file with the Clients .dbf
                database file and form a new database file, Newlist, to include first
                and last names, addresses, and the cost of trips .

                    SELECT 2
                    USE Clients

                    SELECT 1
                    USE Travel


                In the following JOIN command example, Newlist is the new .dbf
                file created with the fields Firstname, Lastname, City, and Cost from
                the two database files, Travel .dbf and Clients .dbf . Because Address
                and City are fields found only in Clients, which is in the unselected
                work area, you have to let dBASE III PLUS know where to find
                these fields . You can identify fields in work area 1 by the alias A or
                Travel, or work area 2 by the alias B or clients .

LABEL FORM        LABEL FORM uses a specified label format file designed with MOD-
                  IFY LABEL to print or display labels .

Syntax            LABEL FORM < label filename > /? [ < scope > ] [SAMPLE]
                  [WHILE < condition > ] [FOR < condition > ]
                  [TO PRINT/TO FILE < filename > ]

Defaults          File names must include the drive designator if the file is not
                  on the default drive, unless a path is specified. If no file extension
                  is specified in the label filename, dBASE III PLUS assumes an
                  .lbl extension.
                  If no file extension is specified in the TO FILE filename,
                  dBASE III PLUS assumes a .txt extension . Unless otherwise speci-
                  fied by the scope, the WHILE or FOR clause, or an active filter,
                  labels are printed for all records in the active database file .

Options           Use the SAMPLE option to print test labels to ensure proper align-
                  ment of the labels in the printer . The process may be repeated as
                  many times as necessary by responding Y when asked Do you want
                  more samples? When you respond with N, labels begin printing .
                  The TO FILE option is used to send the labels to a standard ASCII
                  text file .
                  Use the catalog query clause to activate a menu of all label files for
                  the active database file .

Tip               When printing labels, make sure that the labels are in the printer
                  and the printer is turned on before issuing the command . If the
                  printer is not on, the command will not be executed immediately .
                  After a short pause, the labels will be displayed on your screen . If
                  you realize your printer is not on after you issue the command and
                  you turn it on immediately, the labels will begin printing.

See Also          CREATE/MODIFY LABEL
