GLOSSARY

Cursor Control    The menu of navigation keys. Pressing F1 toggles this menu on and
Menu              off in full-screen operations such as EDIT and BROWSE .

dBASE             The programming language built into dBASE III PLUS .

DBMS              An acronym for DataBase Management System .

Data Disk         A disk containing the database, index, format, and other files used
                  by dBASE III PLUS .

Data Type         One of the five types of data that can be entered in a database file :
                  character (C), numeric (N), logical (L), date (D), or memo (M) .
                  Memory variables also have data types, but no equivalent to memo
                  (M) .

Database          A file or group of files containing records of related data . The
                  database may also include any ancillary files to the database files
                  such as index, report, and query files .

Database          The accuracy of the data in a database .
Integrity

Debug             To find and correct errors in a software program

Decrement         To decrease a value, or the amount by which a value is decreased .

Default           The preset or automatic value of an option in the absence of a dif-
                  ferent specification . Defaults in dBASE III PLUS environments are
                  usually changed with a SET command . Command defaults are usu-
                  ally changed by a scope or conditional clause .

Definition        A filename in a list of input files that dBCODE and dBLINKER use
                  in processing .




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                                           UG- 5
                                                                                   GLOSSARY


Delimiters          Characters used to enclose character data items . Character data is
                    normally delimited with single or double quotation marks (for
                    example, STORE 'Hello' TO X) . Square brackets are also valid
                    delimiters in dBASE III PLUS . Commas are used to separate data
                    items in a list (for example, DISPLAY Name,Address,City,State), or
                    to separate fields in a text file . When used to separate fields in a text
                    file, the comma is properly called a field separator .

Descending          The order from the highest to the lowest value (for example, Z to A
Order               and 9 to 0) . In dBASE III PLUS, descending order for character
                    data is determined by reverse ASCII order . See Appendix D for a list
                    of ASCII character codes .

Device              Any part of the computer that is capable of sending or receiving
                    information . The keyboard is an example of an input device ; the
                    video monitor and printer are output devices .

Directory           A catalog of files on a disk .

DOS                 An acronym for Disk Operating System . Often used to refer to the
                    PC-DOS or MS-DOS operating system .

Dot Prompt          The dBASE III PLUS prompt, represented by a dot (.) on the screen
                    (unless changed in the Config .db file) . This is also known as the
                    interactive mode, as opposed to the full-screen mode . Editing capa-
                    bilities such as inserting, deleting, and overwriting are available at
                    the dot prompt .

Drive               Indicates the disk drive identifier (for example, A, B, or C) . When
                    used as part of a filename, the disk drive identifier must be followed
                    by a colon (for example, A:) .

Encrypt             To make program code or a database file unreadable by others so
                    that it cannot be modified or otherwise tampered with . The
                    dBCODE portion of RunTime + encrypts dBASE program files .

End-of-File (EOF)   A location after the last physical record .




UG-6                                                                   USING dBASE III PLUS
GLOSSARY


Enhanced           An attribute of the monitor display used by some dBASE III PLUS
                   commands . This appears on a monochrome monitor as black fore-
                   ground on a white background . See Standard .

Enter              Used in two contexts : (1) to type in a command or data in response
                   to a prompt message, and (2) a synonym for the RETURN key .

Enumerated Value   One of a fixed number of possible values for a menu option . For
                   example, one of the five possible field types that can be assigned
                   while creating a database file, or the ON/OFF values in the SET
                   Menu .

Environment        See Working Environment .

Error Trapping     Refers to routines set up in programs to check for and correct
                   potential user errors .

Esc                See Escape Key .

Escape Code        A symbol used to instruct a printer to print in a special mode, such
                   as expanded print mode, by combining of the ASCII code for Esc
                   (Decimal Code 27), with one or more other ASCII codes .

Escape Key         The key used in dBASE III PLUS to abandon program or command
                   execution .

Exp                See Expression.

Expression         A combination of constants, variables, and operators that produces
                   a result of a single data type, that is, numeric, character, logical, or
                   date . The type of an expression is defined by the type of result that
                   it returns . Dates may enter into expressions with numbers (addition
                   and subtraction) to form date expressions . One date may be sub-
                   tracted from another to form a numeric expression . The letters C,
                   D, L, or N may be used after the abbreviation to indicate the data
                   type of the expression . For example, < expC > indicates a charac-
                   ter expression .




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                   UG- 7
                                                                                 GLOSSARY


Expression List   An expression list consists of one or more expressions . If more than
                  one expression is present, they must be separated by commas . The
                  expressions do not have to be the same data type .

Extension         A period and up to three characters added to the end of a filename
                  that can be used to identify the type of file . In the sample file
                  Clients .dbf, the extension is .dbf, which stands for "database file ."
                  The extension is also called a file identifier .

Field             An individual data item in a record within a database file .

Field List        A listing of field names separated by commas .

Field Name        The name assigned to a field . A field name may have up to 10 char-
                  acters consisting of letters, numbers, and underscores . It must
                  begin with a letter and cannot contain embedded blank spaces .

Field Type        Indicates the type of data that may be stored within a field . Field
                  types are character (C), date (D), logical (L), memo (M), and
                  numeric (N) .

Field Width       The number of character spaces assigned to a field .

File              A collection of related information . When used within a command,
                  FILE followed by a filename indicates that the command is to apply
                  to the entire file (for example, DELETE FILE Garbage .dbf) .

Filename          The name of a disk file, which may consist of up to eight characters
                  and may be followed by an optional period and a three-letter exten-
                  sion . It must begin with a letter and cannot contain an embedded
                  blank space . Do not use the single letters A through J or M as
                  filenames .

File Type         An aspect of a file describing its structure or contents, or the func-
                  tion it performs with a program . File types are often identified by
                  the three-character extension following the filename and a period .
                  For example, in dBASE III PLUS, database files are assigned an
                  extension of .dbf to indicate they hold data .




UG-8                                                               USING dBASE III PLUS
GLOSSARY


Filter            An expression that limits the data used in commands that require a
                  database ( .dbf) file to be in USE . It does not alter the size of the file .

FOR               An optional clause in many commands which indicates that the
< condition >     command is to apply to every record in the database for which the
                  scope of the condition is True .

Foreground        The characters that appear on the monitor against the background .
                  See Background.

Form Feed         An action represented by ASCII code 12 that causes the paper in a
                  printer to advance to the top of the next page . The EJECT command
                  causes a form feed .

Full-Screen       A dBASE III PLUS command that occupies the entire monitor
Command           screen with menu, help, or message text while the command is in
                  progress . EDIT and The Assistant (ASSIST) are full-screen
                  commands .

Function          Part of the dBASE command language . A function accepts
                  arguments of a particular type and returns data of a specified type .
                  A function is an expression the type of which is defined by its result .

Hard Carriage     ASCII code 13 . It is equivalent to a carriage return and line feed .
Return

Header            Information at the beginning of a database file that allows
                  dBASE III PLUS to maintain the file, such as the file type and the
                  number of fields and records (see Appendix C) .

Hidden Variable   A PUBLIC variable the value of which is hidden from a subprogram
                  when a PRIVATE variable is created with the same name . When
                  program flow returns to the calling program, the original PUBLIC
                  variable is reinstated .

Highlight         An inverse video bar that surrounds the text of the current option
                  on a menu .




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                      UG- 9
                                                                               GLOSSARY

History           A feature that retains command lines typed at the dot prompt or
                  executed in a program file and allows them to be recalled and
                  reused or (if entered at the dot prompt) edited . The command lines
                  are stored in a memory buffer called the history buffer, which
                  stores the last 20 lines unless its size is modified in Config .db or
                  with SET HISTORY TO .

Hook              Files named in a DO < filename > statement but not provided to
                  dBLINKER for processing . RunTime + does not alter these unde-
                  fined references, allowing easy modification of applications .

Horizontal        A way to allow input of data into a . . . GET field or entry area of a
Scrolling         menu when the data is longer than the blank . This is done with the
                  S <n> template function for the     command, and occurs auto-
                  matically in menus .

Housekeeping      Those functions necessary to the operation of a computer but not
                  directly related to the program in progress . Examples of housekeep-
                  ing include opening and closing files, clearing memory, and verifi-
                  cation functions .

I/O               Abbreviation for input/output . A disk drive is an example of an
                  input/output device .

Increment         To increase a value, or the amount by which a value is increased .

Inactive Option   An option that cannot be selected from a menu because circum-
                  stances make it inappropriate .

Index File        A special-purpose file that relates a key (an item of particular inter-
                  est to the user) to a database record number . Index keys are in
                  ascending order .

Initialize        To set up memory variables by STOREing data in a named variable .

Input             The transfer of data into the CPU or RAM of the computer, such as
                  input from the keyboard .

Instruction       A command or program step telling the computer exactly what to
                  do for a particular operation .

GLOSSARY

Integer            A number with no fractional part ; a whole number .

Interpreter        The part of dBASE III PLUS which parses commands and performs
                   them .

Interrupt          To prematurely stop a program or operation in progress .

Install            To transfer a functional copy of dBASE III PLUS to a disk other
                   than the original system disk . Installing is automated by use of the
                   INSTALL batch program on System Disk #1 .

Interactive        Requiring the participation of the user . Interactive commands or
                   programs issue prompts and accept input.

Inverse Video      Displaying text on the monitor by using dark letters against a light
                   background. Also referred to as reverse video .

Key                A field or expression value by which a database file is INDEXed or
                   SORTed.

Key Expression     An expression used to INDEX or SORT a database file .

Key Field          A field which is used alone, or as part of a key expression, to
                   INDEX or SORT a database file .

Leading Blanks     The blank spaces preceding the first non-blank character in a char-
                   acter variable .

Linking            Using dBLINKER to join encrypted program modules (except pro-
                   cedure files) to create a finished, complete program . Also used to
                   describe the process of setting a relation between database files .

literal            An explicit representation to be taken at face value ; a word, num-
                   ber, or symbol that describes or defines itself and not something
                   else that it might represent . Literals are never delimited .

logical Operator   One of the operators .AND., .OR ., or .NOT . used to relate logical
                   expressions.

Logical Order      The order of records based on an index file .

                                                                                GLOSSARY


Log-in Code       A code used to identify a particular user to the system and allow
                  entry .

Looping           The repeated execution of a series of commands while a given con-
                  dition is True .

Macro             A single word or symbol that substitutes for a group of commands
                  or an entire subroutine . The ampersand (&) is the macro function .
                  It substitutes the contents of a memory variable in those cases

Main Program      The highest-level calling program in a dBASE programming
                  application .

Master Catalog    A special catalog file, automatically created and maintained in the

Memory Variable   An identifiable data item that is not part of a database file but is

Memvar            An abbreviation for memory variable . It normally indicates that the

Memvar List       Consists of one or more memory variable names . If more than

                  commas .

Menu              A list of options .
Menu-assisted     Used to describe commands that have an optional menu .

Menu-driven       The process that allows users to select a course of action based

                  are examples of menu-driven commands .

Monitor           The video display device or video screen .

GLOSSARY

Multi-user          A system that allows two or more users to share the resources of a
                    computer, its peripherals, and in some cases, its data.

n                   Indicates a number . In most cases, a numeric expression (such as
                    cost * percentage) may be used as well as a literal number (such
                    as 5) .

Nest                In programming, putting a control structure, such as a
                    DO WHILE . . . ENDDO or IF . . . ENDIF construction, within another

Network             A group of computer work stations linked to a common processor
                    or file server .

Numeric Fields      Fields containing numbers that may be directly used in mathemati-

Pan                 To move off-screen information into view in BROWSE and other
                    commands .

                    3 . PARAMETERS is also a command that allows a subroutine to
                       access field names, memory variables, and expressions passed to
                       it with a DO command.

Parameter Passing   Giving a set of variables to another program for use in that
                    program . See Parameter .

Parse                The initial test dBASE III PLUS does on a command line to verify
                     the correct syntax of the command .

Password             An identifying code word that allows a user access to a system or
                     file.

Path                 Refers to the specified search pattern to locate files not on the cur-
                     rent directory .

Prefix               A (possibly null) text string affixed before a filename . This may be
                     used to specify a drive and/or subdirectory, such as
                     A: < filename > .

Print                Indicates output to the printer within a command . T O PRINT is an
                     optional part of certain commands that turns the printer on only
                     while the command is active. The printer can also be turned on and
                     off by means of the SET PRINT and SET DEVICE commands .

Procedure            A special type of dBASE III PLUS program or subroutine . A proce-
                     dure file may contain up to 32 routines (called procedures), each
                     beginning with the word PROCEDURE.

Procedure File       A special type of dBASE III PLUS command file . It may contain up
                     to 32 procedures . Its function is to combine several related com-
                     mand files into one file .

Program              A set of instructions or steps designed to have the computer per-
                     form a specific sequence of actions ; an application developed in the
                     dBASE programming language .

Programming          A way to set up commands in special files without having to retype
                     the commands each time they are needed.

Programming          A special set of syntax rules and commands that tells the computer
Language             what to do and in what sequence .

Prompt               A symbol, word, or phrase that is used to indicate the computer's
                     readiness to accept input from the user and the input expected .

GLOSSARY

Pseudo-Code       A way of writing programs that incorporates both English and
                  actual program commands as a method of clarifying program struc-
                  ture during the design stage of a programming project .

Pull-Down Menu    A menu that displays selection options for its related heading dis-
                  played on the menu bar .

Query             A specific request for data or instructions .

Query Clause      See the entry under "?" .

Record            A group of related fields of information treated as a unit . Also, one
                  complete horizontal row in a rectangular table of rows and
                  columns .

Record Count      The total number of records in a database file .

Record Number     A unique identifying number assigned by dBASE III PLUS to each
                  record in a database .

Record Pointer    A number used by dBASE III PLUS to identify the current database
                  record .

Reference         The file named in a DO < filename > statement .

Relation          A connection established between multiple database files by using a
                  key field or expression as a common reference point .

Relational        A system that allows data to be accessed based on relationships
Database System   which are set up among several database files .

Relative          Using row and column positions that relate to the previous position
Addressing        on the screen or printer without using specific coordinate numbers .

Routine           A set of commands that performs a particular operation .

Row               A number indicating the vertical position on either the video moni-
                  tor or the printed page . Rows are numbered from top to bottom ;
                  the top line on both devices is row 0 . When referring to the printer,
                  the word line is used synonymously with row .


USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                UG- 1 5
                                                                                GLOSSARY


RunTime +           The dBASE III PLUS system for creating commercial applications .
                    RunTime + includes dBCODE for compiling command and proce-
                    dure files, and dBLINKER for joining these files into a single file .

Run-Time Error      A mistake in programming logic that generally doesn't appear until
                    the program is run .

Scope               An optional part of many commands that specifies the amount of
                    the database file to which the command applies . Each command
                    which has the SCOPE option has a default of either the current
                    database record or all database records . The scope may be :
                    RECORD N - a single record ; NEXT N - n records beginning
                    with the current record ; ALL - all of the records in the database
                    file; or REST - from the current record to the end of the file .

Scoreboard          Information that is pertinent to data entry, such as insert and over-
                    write status, or the deletion status of records . Scoreboard informa-
                    tion is displayed either on the status bar in full-screen commands,
                    or at the top of the screen when working from the dot prompt with
                    SET STATUS OFF .

Screen              Any display seen on the monitor . Also, a particular image that may
                    be referenced .

Screen Form         A customized screen entry form used to receive user input . Screen
                    forms generally replace those supplied by default in the full-screen
                    commands, such as APPEND or EDIT .

Screen Painter      A feature in dBASE III PLUS that allows users to create customized
                    screen forms easily without knowing specific row and column coor-
                    dinates .

Sector              In MS-DOS, disks are divided into logical areas called sectors . Each
                    sector contains a block of 512 bytes . The COPY FILE command
                    transfers data in sectors rather than by individual bytes . This means
                    that the file created will only contain complete 512-byte blocks,
                    even if the last block is only partially filled .

Sequential Access   A method by which the database is searched in consecutive order
                    until the desired record is located .



UG- 1 6                                                             USING dBASE III PLUS
GLOSSARY


Setup Area        The part of the main program that determines the working environ-
                  ment of the program .

Single-user       That version of dBASE III PLUS configured for use on stand- alone
                  microcomputer systems .

Skeleton          The mask or template used to define filenames and memory vari-
                  able names that have common elements . A skeleton makes use of
                  the ? and the * to "wildcard" parts of these names with common
                  elements . For example, DIR * .ndx will display the names of all
                  index files .
                  The * applies to several characters . The ? wildcards individual char-
                  acters . To illustrate, DIR ??SE .* will display the names of files
                  where the filename is four characters long and ends in SE with any
                  file extension .

Soft Carriage     A character automatically inserted at the end of a text line, which
Return            the editor regards as a carriage return . Also referred to as
                  wrap-around.

Sort              To rearrange information in a logical sequence such as alphabetical
                  or numeric order . In dBASE III PLUS, a new database file is cre-
                  ated with records in the sorted order .

Standard          An attribute of the monitor display used by most dBASE III PLUS
                  commands . On a monochrome monitor this appears as a white fore-
                  ground on a black background .

Status Bar        A line at the bottom of the screen containing information about the
                  current session, such as the file being used and the default disk
                  drive.

String            See Character String .

Structured        The art of writing program modules such that each module accom-
Programming       plishes one specific task in the program .

Submenu           A list of options that appear as a result of a menu selection .




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                UG- 1 7
                                                                              GLOSSARY

Subroutine        A program which is called by another program and dependent on it .

Substring         A portion or subset of a string .

Syntax            The rules governing the structure of a command .

Template          A mask to aid, define, or limit the entry of data . The template
                  99/99/99 can be used as an aid in entering dates into a character
                  variable, for example .

TO                A part of many dBASE III PLUS commands that indicates the target
                  of the command . T O is normally followed by either a filename or a
                  memory variable name . Some commands use TO as a natural con-
                  nector to specify a processing characteristic (for example, SET
                  COLOR TO) .

Toggle            A switch that is always in one of two different states . For example,
                  the cursor control menu is toggled on and off using F1 .

Top-Down Design   A way of designing programs starting with an initial concept and
                  then breaking the program down into specific parts or modules .

Trailing Blanks   The blank spaces following the last non-blank character in a charac-
                  ter variable, to the length of the field .

Truncate          To drop or trim digits from numbers or characters in a character
                  string. For example, the number 4 .342 can be truncated to 4 .

Turnkey System    A program which begins automatically when the user turns on the
                  computer and which cushions the user from the actual working of
                  the computer .

Type-ahead        An area that stores keyboard input until dBASE III PLUS is able to
Buffer            respond to this input .

Uninstall         To copy dBASE III PLUS from a secondary disk back to its original
                  system disk . Uninstalling is done with the UNINSTAL batch
                  program .




UG- 1 8                                                           USING dBASE III PLUS
GLOSSARY

User-defined       Values that must be entered by the user .
Values

User Interface     The software mechanism by which users access, respond to, and
                   control an application program . The user interface includes screen
                   forms, prompts, messages, and help .

Variable           A symbol with a value that may change during program
                   execution .

View               A selective way to look into a set of files . A view is itself a special
                   file that sets relations between database files and selects the fields
                   that may be accessed .

WHILE             An optional clause in many commands which indicates that the
< condition >     command is to be repeated as long as the stated condition is True .
                  When WHILE < condition > is used with a command that applies
                  to database records (such as LIST), each record is evaluated in
                  sequence and the command terminates when either the condition is
                  False or the scope is exceeded .

Wildcard          A symbol that permits substitution for individual characters or
                  groups of characters in variable names and filenames . The wildcard
                  substitution for individual characters is the question mark (?) . For
                  groups of characters it is the asterisk (*) .

Work Area         dBASE III PLUS is divided into ten independent work areas, each
                  one capable of containing one database file, its associated index
                  files, a format file, a filter, and a linkage to another work area .

Workstation       A computer terminal, usually part of a Local Area Network, at
                  which work is done . Workstations are linked to a central processor
                  or file server .

Working           The way an application program handles the screen, database files,
Environment       and disk space during the run of the program . The working environ-
                  ment may be different from the default working environment of
                  dBASE III PLUS at the dot prompt .




USING dBASE III PLUS                                                                    UG- 1 9
                                                                   GLOSSARY

Zoom      A feature that allows constricted data entry areas to expand
          to 80-column width for easier reading . Zoom is toggled on by
          Ctrl-PgDn and toggled off by Ctrl-PgUp .
